**Proposition.** *Let $A$ be an algebra over a commutative ring $R$ generated by $\sigma_0, \sigma_1$ subject to the relations of $H_3(q)$, with $h = q - q^{-1}$. Let $t : A \to R$ be $R$-linear with $t(xy) = t(yx)$. Let $\theta$ be the anti-automorphism that exchanges $\sigma_0 \leftrightarrow \sigma_1$ and reverses products. For every product $x = f_1 \cdots f_m$ of factors $f_k = \alpha_k + \beta_k \sigma_{i_k}$,*

$$
  t(\theta(x)) = t(x).
$$

The factors include $\sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - h$, every typed crossing operator $C(f, f'; \sigma_i)$ of [the typed crossing operator](#def:typed-crossing-operator), and their inverses. A Markov trace is such a $t$.

**Proof.** The exchange is inner. With $\Delta = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0$, the braid relation gives $\Delta\sigma_0 = \sigma_1\Delta$ and $\Delta\sigma_1 = \sigma_0\Delta$, and $\Delta$ is invertible with inverse $\sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}$. So $t$ of the exchanged product equals $t(\Delta x \Delta^{-1}) = t(x)$.

For reversal, every product of factors reduces to a combination of the six elements $1, \sigma_0, \sigma_1, \sigma_0\sigma_1, \sigma_1\sigma_0, \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0$. The relations $\sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + 1$ and $\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 = \sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1$ read the same backwards. Multiplying on the right in the original order and on the left in the reversed order therefore produces the same coefficients, with $\sigma_0\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_1\sigma_0$ exchanged. A cyclic trace gives $t(\sigma_0\sigma_1) = t(\sigma_1\sigma_0)$. $\square$

**Consequence.** Every typed nucleon word whose flavour assignment is carried to another one by $\theta$ has the same trace as that word. In particular this holds for the six placements of the odd quark on $(\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3$. A difference between proton and neutron therefore requires an ingredient that is not a cyclic trace of such a product.

The same Lean file also records three smaller statements:
- the switched photon $1 + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}$ equals the [photon](#def:photon) $\gamma(\varphi_0 - h\varphi_{01},\, \varphi_1,\, \varphi_{01})$, so switched and unswitched photons are the same family, and the two factors of [the two-photon factorisation](#prop:borromean-two-photon-factorisation) are switched photons with only their last term;
- commuting separators can be moved past a photon;
- on a $2 \times 2$ representation in which $\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}$ has no fixed vector and is not a scalar, its trace is $-(1 + h^2)$ and its determinant is $1$.
